A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoboRefer and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. v1 Appendices A–H correspond to v2 Appendices B–I; v2 adds a Discussion appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, simulation and real-world robot evaluations, and ablations in Tables 1–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds reasoning-length, backbone-transfer, and depth-source comparisons in Tables 8–10.

M1.justification: The separate RGB/depth encoders, point outputs, two-step SFT, and GRPO training with outcome and process rewards remain unchanged. The additional backbone experiment does not establish a revision to RoboRefer’s proposed architecture or training algorithm.

E1.justification: The training corpora, spatial and general benchmarks, Open6DOR V2 position track, and UR5/G1 tasks are retained. Added analyses use existing coverage with different backbone or depth-processing settings.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated SpatialRGPT-8B, which v1 cited but omitted from this comparison. New Table 9 also compares RefSpatial-finetuned Qwen-2.5-VL-7B with its base model and the NVILA/RoboRefer models.

E3.justification: v2 adds partial RefSpatial fine-tuning of Qwen-2.5-VL-7B and a controlled comparison of estimated versus camera depth. Section 3.4 changes the optional depth-estimator citation from UniDepth V2 to DepthAnything V2, and Section 4.2 specifies default RGB-D evaluation. The PDFs do not establish reruns of retained results.

E4.justification: New Tables 8–10 analyze final success by required reasoning length, transfer of RefSpatial training to another backbone, and sensitivity to depth source. These substantially broaden the diagnostic scope beyond v1’s data-mixture, encoder, and reward ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run/seed reporting. The new analyses do not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing main-table RoboRefer scores are retained. v2 adds SpatialRGPT scores and the results in Tables 8–10; for example, apple-placement success is 60% with DepthAnything V2 versus 40% with camera depth. The new reasoning-length rates in Table 8 do not aggregate to its totals using Table 11’s listed sample counts.

T1.justification: The task and reasoning-step definitions, SFT loss, GRPO sampling, reward thresholds, and advantage equations are retained. The added depth-to-3D discussion clarifies practical assumptions without introducing new formal mathematics or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: RoboRefer, RefSpatial, RefSpatial-Bench, and improved spatial understanding and referring. The headline 89.6% average and 17.4-point advantage claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds backbone-selection rationale, an interpretation of depth-noise robustness, and qualifications concerning calibrated depth-to-3D mapping and partial observations. The conclusion adds direct quantitative 3D reasoning as future work. The human-intent limitation already appeared in v1 and is retained.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies DepthAnything V2 for default inference-depth generation and newly documents FoundationStereo use under severe real-world depth noise. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, data-processing instructions, and access links are retained; the new Qwen experiment is described only as partial training.

R1.justification: v2 adds 17 cited works, including DepthAnything V2, MoGe-2, and FoundationStereo. Appendix A provides a focused comparison with SpatialRGPT across task requirements, model usage, data construction, and training, while preserving the paper’s overall positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds Discussion Appendix A, expands the conclusion with future work, adds acknowledgements, and updates affiliations and contact text. Existing appendices are renumbered, with limited prose revisions and most narrative structure retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–10 and a SpatialRGPT row in Table 1, revises coordinate annotations in Figure 2, and reflows existing material. v1 Tables 8–10 become Tables 11–13, and the existing figure collection is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful comparisons and makes depth-related applicability limits more explicit. However, its new Table 8 conflicts with the retained benchmark counts in Table 11: weighting the Location-SFT subgroup rates yields 42.77%, versus the reported 47.00%. The benefits coexist with unresolved reliability problems in the added reasoning evidence, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
